# Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0511a)

**ID:** Atk S0511a
**Section:** Aṭṭhakathā Khuddakanikāya (atk-s05)
**Collection:** Atthakatha-Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā
**Title (English, from literature):** The Clarifier of the Sweet Meaning
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā*, traditionally titled *Madhuratthavilāsinī* (or *Maduratthavilāsinī*), is the commentary on the *Buddhavaṃsa* within the Khuddakanikāya commentary collection [Phaengcharoen 2006; Endo 1997]. It provides an extensive narrative framework for the lineage of past Buddhas and Gotama Buddha, setting out doctrinal analyses such as the ten perfections (*pāramī*) [Endo 1997] and detailing the chronology of the first twenty years of Gotama Buddha's teaching career and summer retreats [Gethin 1998]. The commentary preserves notable narrative variants: for instance, it recounts only three omens seen by Prince Siddhattha before his renunciation, leaving out the corpse described in most other commentaries [Adikaram 1946], and explains that the six-colored rays emitted during the Twin Miracle derive from *kasiṇa* meditation [Zhu 2017]. In its commentarial method, it incorporates the *sambahulavāra* (manifold section), adding ten descriptive sections to the canonical *Buddhavaṃsa*'s twenty categories for each Buddha [Adikaram 1946].

The Pali Text Society edition of the text was prepared by I. B. Horner, who finished editing it during the air raids of World War II and published it in 1946 [Cousins et al. 1974; Masefield 1994]. Horner later translated the work into English under the title *The Clarifier of the Sweet Meaning*, published by the Pali Text Society in 1978 [Endo 1997].

**Sources**

- [Phaengcharoen 2006] Phramaha Somphong Santacitto Phaengcharoen, Analytical Study of Concept of Dhamma as Natural Law in Theravada (2006) — Attestation of title Madhuratthavilāsinī and Horner's edition
- [Endo 1997] Toshiichi Endo, Buddha in Theravada Buddhism: A Study of the Concept of Buddha in the Pali Commentaries (1997) — English translation title by I. B. Horner, discussion of the perfections, and alternate spelling Maduratthavilāsinī
- [Zhu 2017] Tianshu Zhu, Buddhas and Bodhisattvas: Emanators and Emanated Beings in Buddhist Art of Gandhara, Central Asia, and China (2017) — Details on the Buddha's rays during the Twin Miracle and kasiṇa meditation
- [Cousins et al. 1974] L. Cousins, A. Kunst, and K. R. Norman, eds., Buddhist Studies in Honour of I.B. Horner (1974) — Context of I. B. Horner's PTS edition completed during World War II
- [Masefield 1994] Peter Masefield, Divine Revelation in Pali Buddhism (1979, 1994) — Publication date of Horner's PTS edition (1946)
- [Adikaram 1946] E. W. Adikaram, Early History of Buddhism in Ceylon (1946) — Commentarial method of sambahulavāra and omission of the corpse among the signs
- [Gethin 1998] Rupert Gethin, The Foundations of Buddhism (1998) — Account of the first twenty years of the Buddha's teaching career
- [Tournier et al.] Vincent Tournier, in Archaeologies of the Written (eds. Tournier, Eltschinger, Sernesi) — Parallel list of retreats in Sengqieluocha suoji jing
